description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Electrical Measurements and Instrumentation topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: electrical-measurements

facts.claim: Accuracy = closeness to the true value; precision = closeness to each other

source.quote: accuracy is how close a given set of measurements is to the true value and precision is how close the measurements are to each other
two distinct types of errors, systematic errors on the one hand, and random on the other hand

facts.claim: Random errors are reduced by repeating measurements

source.quote: The effects of random errors can be mitigated by repeated measurements

facts.claim: A coil in a permanent magnet's field deflects a pointer with current

source.quote: Galvanometers work by deflecting a pointer in response to an electric current flowing through a coil in a constant magnetic field

facts.claim: An ammeter is connected in series and has low resistance

source.quote: Ammeters must be connected in series with the circuit to be measured

facts.claim: Low resistance so it barely changes the circuit

source.quote: An ammeter usually has low resistance so that it does not cause a significant voltage drop

facts.claim: Balanced when no current flows through the galvanometer

source.quote: The resistance R2 is adjusted until the bridge is "balanced" and no current flows through the galvanometer
used to measure an unknown electrical resistance by balancing two legs of a bridge circuit

facts.claim: Maxwell bridge measures an unknown inductance

source.quote: A Maxwell bridge is a modification to a Wheatstone bridge used to measure an unknown inductance

facts.claim: Fixed current coils and a moving potential (pressure) coil

source.quote: a pair of fixed coils, known as current coils, and a movable coil known as the potential coil

facts.claim: It reads average power V I cos φ

source.quote: which in sinusoidal steady-state reduces to Vrms Irms cos(φ)
the most common one being the kilowatt hour (kWh)

facts.claim: A potentiometer compares an unknown voltage with a known reference (null method)

source.quote: by comparison of an unknown voltage with a known reference voltage

facts.claim: At balance it draws (almost) no current from the source

source.quote: very little current is drawn from the source of the unknown voltage

facts.claim: A CT gives a secondary current proportional to the primary current

source.quote: producing a current in its secondary which is proportional to the current in its primary

facts.claim: Instrument transformers scale large values to small standard ones

source.quote: scale the large values of voltage or current to small, standardized values

facts.claim: An ADC converts an analog voltage to a digital number

source.quote: converts an analog input voltage or current to a digital number

facts.claim: A multimeter measures voltage, current and resistance

source.quote: A typical multimeter can measure voltage, resistance, and current

facts.claim: A transducer converts energy (signal) from one form to another

source.quote: A transducer is a device that usefully converts energy from one form to another
